## My Reasoning

I've been farming this land in Quzhou for over 40 years. My father farmed it before me. I know what this soil and this climate will support, and I know what the market wants. The answer has always been the same, and it remains the same: **winter wheat followed by summer maize** on the same 10 mu.

Some younger farmers in the village have experimented with vegetables or cotton, but at my age and with just myself and my wife managing things, I need crops I can mechanize entirely. I'm not breaking my back at 63. The wheat-maize rotation fits the machinery I own, the skills I have, and the buyers at the county grain station who've been taking my harvest reliably for two decades.

Water is my biggest concern. I've watched the well levels drop every year. Quzhou sits on a shrinking aquifer — the agricultural institute people have been telling us this for 20 years and I believe them now. So for the wheat I'll do three irrigations instead of the four my father always did: the pre-sowing moisture irrigation before planting in October, then jointing in April, then heading in May. I'm skipping the grain-filling irrigation — the variety I'm using, Jimai 22, can handle it if I time the heading irrigation right.

For maize I plant directly after wheat harvest in mid-June with a no-tillage seeder. Summer rain in Quzhou usually handles most water needs. I'll irrigate at emergence if the ground is dry, and again at silking if July is bad. Two irrigations, maybe one.

I use improved wheat seed — not hybrid, wheat doesn't work that way — and Xianyu 335 hybrid maize, the same I've used for eight years. It performs. I don't chase new varieties every season like some people. My fertilizer rates have come down slightly from what I used in my 40s; the soil organic matter has built up with the straw incorporation, and I don't want to spend money I don't need to spend.

Pesticides: three passes on wheat (seed treatment for fusarium, a herbicide spray in winter, and a fungicide-insecticide combined spray at heading for rust and aphids). Two passes on maize (herbicide at emergence, and one insecticide spray if corn borer pressure is high, which it has been recent years).

I'll do rotary tillage before wheat seeding in October to incorporate the maize stover. Deep ploughing I do every three years — did it last autumn, so not this year.
